research_notes: A future cost model can balance checkpoint overhead against expected lost-tail work from abrupt termination.
Near a reliable cap with low failure probability, checkpoint cadence may be relaxed.
Near an uncertain boundary, denser checkpoints reduce experimental and operational loss.
This suggests checkpoint cadence may be phase-dependent even if the runtime cap is fixed.
Such adaptation is simpler than full runtime-cap adaptation and may have practical value.
It remains a later supporting optimization.
